title: Competition for the Same Target In Vivo
content: For a deeper and more comprehensive study of this topic, the author proposed the competition coefficient (Rc) and, on its basis, the competition rule. In the body, competition phenomena can be observed not only with respect to a drug substance, but also with respect to other substances capable of binding to blood proteins. Using the law of competition for binding to the same target in vivo, the following were investigated: - competition between exogenous ligands (drugs), - competition between endogenous (natural) ligands, - competition between endogenous and exogenous ligands. The aim of the study was to determine the relationships between the competition coefficient (Rc) and binding affinity, therapeutic effect, side effects, physiological activity (potency), selectivity (main effect) and duration of action (T1/2), etc. The article presents the results of extensive statistical research, analysis and interpretation. Various tables and diagrams are used for a clear presentation of the material. The study showed that an increase in the competition coefficient (Rc) within one pharmacological group is accompanied by an increase in binding affinity between the ligand and the target molecule, therapeutic effect, selectivity (main effect), duration of action (T1/2) and a decrease in side effects. The author pays considerable attention to confirming the theoretical conclusions of the study by comparing them with already known practical results. The article may be useful for scientific researchers, as well as for teachers, students, clinical specialists and physicians.
